answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy ties each identity to a non-refundable stake on a glacier-slow vesting schedule, so registering a new agent costs the same lock for every key an operator declares. A plume of fabricated personas must each post slashable collateral before earning, and weight per settlement window is capped per island of contiguous key creation. The attacker pays linearly in frozen capital, exposed to slashing and withdrawal cooldowns that block instant recycling, while an honest agent pays the stake once. Mass identity is thus priced at locked value, not free reputation.
